solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cut back primarily on game

indicators.note: back tells us the word for cut is to be read from right to left

parts.note: to lop is to cut off branches

indicators.note: primarily asks for just the opening letter of the word on

explanation.surface: Someone trims a hedge or grass before the match, mainly so play can go on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads the cutting word from right to left; 'primarily' takes O. 'Cut' looks like the definition but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a team sport played on horseback with mallets, so it is a kind of game.

clue.text: Sack Liberal leaving for dire crusade

indicators.note: the Liberal's letter leaves and makes way for the dire word in its place

parts.note: to sack a town is to pillage it
grim means dire or dreadful

explanation.surface: A political story: a Liberal quits the sacking of a party for a terrible campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving for' swaps one L of PILLAGE for GRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey to a holy place; the Crusades were seen as armed pilgrimages.

clue.text: Aquatic plant identified by many around university

indicators.note: around shows the word for many encloses the university's letter

parts.note: lots means many, a great number

explanation.surface: Lots of students at a university have identified a water plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily that grows in ponds and lakes, an aquatic plant.

clue.text: Instrument dismissed husband used to stab Welsh buccaneer

indicators.note: something used to stab is pushed into the body of another word, so these letters go inside

parts.note: Sir Henry Morgan was the notorious Welsh privateer of the Caribbean
a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A sacked husband turns to violence against a Welsh pirate with whatever musical instrument comes to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to stab' puts OUTH inside MORGAN, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ, or harmonica, is a small wind instrument played by blowing across reeds.

clue.text: Old bachelors engineered goal: it's essential to the score

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: engineered means contrived or rearranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Some old bachelors fixed a goal, the one that decides the football score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineered' rearranges GOAL and IT into LIGATO. The score here is a musical score, not a match result.
explanation.definitionFit: Obbligato describes an instrumental part that must not be omitted, an essential element of a musical score.

clue.text: Do not put up with it casually at first!

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means the word not is written bottom to top
at first takes the opening letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: An exasperated command: don't tolerate it, at least not at first!
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns NOT into TON; 'at first' takes I and C from 'it casually'.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa, doh (do) is the keynote of the scale, called the tonic.

clue.text: Acceptable footwear sailor finally carried towards land

parts.note: on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

indicators.note: the footwear carries, i.e. holds, the letter inside it

parts.note: a shoe is an item of footwear

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor finally gets decent shoes and is borne ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried' puts R, the last letter of 'sailor', inside SHOE.
explanation.definitionFit: An onshore wind blows from the sea towards the land.

clue.text: Head of garrison more disposed to accept new infantryman

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of garrison
to accept means to take in, so the new letter goes inside

parts.note: readier means more willing, more disposed to do something

explanation.surface: The garrison commander is keener to take on a fresh foot soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts N inside READIER, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier was originally a soldier who threw grenades; the Grenadier Guards are an infantry regiment.

clue.text: Architect and town planner set up two hospitals

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the letters are written upwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital and SAN is short for sanatorium

explanation.surface: A designer of towns builds two hospitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns H plus SAN round.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash designed Regent's Park and Regent Street in London, working as both architect and planner.

clue.text: It cuts tax, giving rise to unbecoming jocularity

indicators.note: the word it cuts into the tax word, so it sits inside

parts.note: a levy is a tax or charge

explanation.surface: A tax cut sets off some unseemly laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving rise to' is only a link between wordplay and definition; it is not a reversal signal here, though it looks like one in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is a lack of proper seriousness, humour at an inappropriate moment.

clue.text: New puppies possibly born in rubbish receptacle

parts.note: a litter is a batch of newborn animals, puppies being one example
B is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A batch of newborn puppies might end up dumped in the garbage, a grim thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter bin is a public container for throwing away rubbish, i.e. a waste receptacle.

clue.text: They help us to see tiny spots, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer is a word that sounds like another, said aloud

parts.note: specks are tiny spots or particles

explanation.surface: Glasses help us spot tiny specks, so the clue reads like an optician's remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Specs is informal for spectacles, the glasses that help people see clearly.

clue.text: Composer and Arctic explorer in one

parts.note: Sir John Ross (and his nephew James Clark Ross) explored the Arctic
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A man who wrote music and also explored the Arctic, two careers rolled into one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville and William Tell.

clue.text: Like a type of music exam taken after church

indicators.note: taken after places the exam's word after the church's abbreviation

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A music exam sat once the church service is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral describes music written for or sung by a choir, one particular kind of music.

clue.text: Antibody ailing gut badly needs initially

indicators.note: badly signals that the words ailing and gut are mixed up
initially picks out the opening letter of needs

explanation.surface: A sick gut needs antibodies to fight the infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges AILING GUT into AGGLUTINI; 'initially' adds N from 'needs'.
explanation.definitionFit: An agglutinin is an antibody that makes cells or bacteria clump together.

clue.text: Cleaning brass? It's an illegal activity

definitions.meaning: brass is British slang for money, so cleaning it is making dirty money look legitimate
passing criminal proceeds through legitimate accounts is a crime

explanation.surface: Polishing the brass sounds innocent, yet the clue insists it is against the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Money laundering conceals the criminal origin of funds and is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Rock plant lovers mostly want cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated, as in tilled soil, signals the letters are worked over into a new order
mostly means all but the final letter of lovers is used

explanation.surface: Gardeners in love would mostly like to grow things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the S of LOVERS; 'cultivated' rearranges LOVER plus WANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Navelwort, or pennywort, grows in rock crevices and walls, a typical rock plant.

clue.text: Man decapitated before autumn, when it gets dark

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the opening letter, is cut off

parts.note: a knight is a man in chess
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A grisly tale of a man beheaded before autumn arrives, after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' drops the K of KNIGHT, a chess piece or 'man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is the onset of night, the time at which darkness comes.

clue.text: Crown representative up north in ravine near choppy lake

indicators.note: in places the words for up and north inside the ravine word

parts.note: a gorge is a narrow steep-sided valley, a ravine
when time is up it is over

indicators.note: choppy water is rough and broken, so the following letters are thrown about

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Directions for a hiker: up north, in a ravine, beside a rough lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' goes inside the ravine word after its first letter; 'choppy' rearranges 'near' to NERA, and L follows. Up = over, as in 'time is up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor-general represents the monarch in a Commonwealth realm such as Canada or Australia.

clue.text: Tease lad eating core of rotting apple

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them

indicators.note: eating means the boy's word takes in the following letter

parts.note: a son is a lad, a boy

indicators.note: core of picks the central letter of rotting

explanation.surface: Mocking a boy who is chewing on the middle of a bad apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts T, the middle of 'rotting', inside SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribston Pippin is an old English dessert apple variety, first grown at Ribston Hall.

clue.text: Having brought up weapon, secure a lump of gold

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the weapon word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
to get something is to secure or obtain it

explanation.surface: A prospector raises a gun to grab a gold nugget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns GUN into NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small natural lump of precious metal, especially gold.

clue.text: One's associated with a former politician's excuses

parts.note: a Lib was a member of the old Liberal Party, now merged into the Liberal Democrats
one is I, so one's (one is) gives I plus S

explanation.surface: Someone is linked to a disgraced ex-politician and needs some excuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Alibis are, loosely, excuses, claims offered to avoid blame.

clue.text: Bones Charlie removed from southern African capital

indicators.note: removed from means one letter is taken out of what follows

parts.note: Accra is the capital of Ghana
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Bones of a man named Charlie removed from a southern African capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' drops one C from S plus ACCRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacra is the plural of sacrum, the triangular bone at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Tower completely infested by nasty bug

indicators.note: a thing infested by bugs has them inside it, so the shuffled letters go within

parts.note: to a T means completely or exactly

indicators.note: nasty signals that the word bug is turned into an unpleasant jumble

explanation.surface: A tower, maybe a castle keep, entirely overrun by a horrible insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' scrambles the insect to UGB, which 'infested by' places after the first T of TO A T. 'Tower' means something that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug tows other vessels, so a tugboat is literally something that tows: a tower.

clue.text: Neat point about turnover of the old plant

indicators.note: about means going round, so the neat-and-point pair surrounds the reversed old word

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
E, east, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: turnover of means the old-style word is turned round

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of the

explanation.surface: A tidy observation about the turnover of old stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover of' reverses the archaic 'the' (ye) and 'about' wraps the cattle and compass letters round it. Neat is an archaic word for cattle, not tidy or undiluted.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye daisy is a common wildflower, a plant.

clue.text: A good universal cure ultimately for malarial fever

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of the word cure

explanation.surface: A sound all-purpose cure, in the end, for malaria.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old name for malaria and its shivering fits.

clue.text: Write someone else's book? That's the spirit

definitions.meaning: to ghostwrite a book published under another's name
the spirit of a dead person

explanation.surface: Offering to write a book for someone else, met with an encouraging 'that's the spirit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosting means writing for another who takes the credit; a ghost is also a spectre or spirit.

clue.text: Tea and fruit taken round east of the Lizard?

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea

indicators.note: the fruit is taken round, i.e. wrapped about, the letter for east

parts.note: a melon is a fruit

explanation.surface: A picnic of tea and fruit on the Lizard, the Cornish peninsula, at its eastern side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' puts E inside MELON. The Lizard is a peninsula in Cornwall, the most southerly point of mainland Britain, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon is a colour-changing reptile, one example of a lizard.

clue.text: Aim to plug old piece of furniture that can be lengthened

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so the aim word is pushed into the furniture word

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Fitting some gadget to an old table that can be pulled out to make it longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to plug' puts the aim word after the first letter of the furniture; 'Aim' is END as in 'ends and means'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extendable means able to be extended, made longer or larger.

clue.text: Useless-sounding vessel

indicators.note: sounding says the answer is spoken the same as another word

parts.note: vain means futile or useless, as in a vain attempt

explanation.surface: A boat that sounds pointless, a vessel as a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein is a blood vessel carrying blood back to the heart.
